name: UserHelp.co
summary: Visual feedback widget for websites: visitors send annotated screenshots and bug reports with browser details, and the paid plan adds session recording, error logs, team collaboration and user forums.
best_for: freelancers, small agencies and site owners who want a feedback button on their websites that collects annotated screenshots and bug reports, and who prefer one payment to a subscription
skip_if: you need documented limits, a refund policy or a support commitment before you buy; or your team already collects website feedback inside its project tool
honest_knock: No refund rule, seat count, recording retention or length of one-time access is stated on the pricing page or in the terms, which date from April 2024. Basic is limited to one project and shows a watermark, and the card does not name its currency. In our test on 18 November 2026 the free plan showed only the 5 oldest responses.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Pro · one-time payment, use on as many sites as you need, no watermark
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-11-26 on userhelp.co/pricing: Basic free and Pro $59 one-time, features unchanged) (read 2026-11-18 on userhelp.co/pricing and in our own test that day; earlier: read 2026-10-17 in a browser; the card shows a $ sign without naming the currency) Two plans, and the page says there are no subscriptions and no per-seat fees. Basic is free forever: unlimited responses, annotated screenshots, response categories, localization and one project, with a UserHelp.co watermark. Pro is $59 one-time: use on as many sites as you need, no watermark, team collaboration, error logs, the browser's technical details, email replies to users, public forums and session recordings. The pricing page does not say how many team members Pro includes, how long session recordings are kept, or how long one-time access lasts, and neither it nor the terms of service (dated 4 April 2024, read in October) state a refund rule. In our test on 18 November 2026 the free plan showed only the 5 oldest responses ('Only the 5 oldest responses are shown'), so Basic collects responses without showing them all; the app also treated categories as a Pro feature although the pricing page lists them on Basic, and it offered an Email add-on with no price shown.

schema_offer.description: Pro, one-time payment, use on as many sites as you need, no watermark; Basic free forever for one project with a watermark; the page shows a $ sign without naming the currency. Read on the vendor's own pricing page on 2026-11-26.

cost_traps.evidence: In our test on 18 November 2026 the free plan showed only the 5 oldest responses ('Only the 5 oldest responses are shown'), so Basic collects responses without showing them all; the app also treated categories as a Pro feature although the pricing page lists them on Basic, and it offered an Email add-on with no price shown.

compare_with.name: BugHerd
compare_with.why: BugHerd is in our dossiers too: point-and-click website feedback for agencies, with Standard at $42 a month billed yearly or $50 month to month for 5 members when we read it on 13 October 2026. UserHelp.co costs $59 once, but publishes far fewer limits and terms.

claims.claim: Upgrade with a one-time payment to view all of them.
claims.observed: The Responses tab on the free plan says that only the 5 oldest responses are shown and offers a one-time payment to see all of them. The dossier says that Free has unlimited responses.
claims.plan: No plan was bought; the Upgrade page was read without clicking the $59 button
claims.comparability: The dossier wording on Free against the notice in the Responses tab of one free project; no report was received, so the table was empty.
claims.buying_consequence: A free user who wants to read all incoming feedback is limited to the first 5 and has to pay.

claims.claim: Free accounts are limited to one project
claims.observed: A second project was refused on the free plan with a notice that the project limit was reached and that unlimited projects need a one-time payment; no second project was made.
claims.plan: No plan was bought; the Upgrade page was read without clicking the $59 button
claims.comparability: The dossier plan wording against the refusal of a second project; the dossier project count for Free was not compared figure by figure.
claims.buying_consequence: A free user can run feedback on one site or product only.

claims.observed: The Upgrade page lists Categories as an upgrade feature, while the dossier puts categories on Free; the Content tab does show an Add category button, and whether it works on the free plan was not tried.
claims.plan: No plan was bought; the Upgrade page was read without clicking the $59 button
claims.comparability: The dossier Free list against the Upgrade page; the Add category button was not used.
claims.buying_consequence: Sorting feedback into categories may need the paid upgrade, against what the dossier says.

claims.observed: The Upgrade page shows an Email add-on with an email inbox, notifications and branded emails, with the line to upgrade your account first and no price. The dossier does not have this add-on.
claims.plan: No plan was bought; the Upgrade page was read without clicking the $59 button
claims.comparability: The Upgrade page add-on against a dossier without it; no price or checkout for it was seen.
claims.buying_consequence: There may be an extra paid add-on on top of the $59 whose price is not shown.

claims.claim: capturing a screenshot is disabled during the preview
claims.observed: The preview of the widget form says that submitting and capturing a screenshot are disabled during the preview and Submit did nothing, so no real report was sent or received.
claims.plan: No plan was bought; the Upgrade page was read without clicking the $59 button
claims.comparability: The widget form preview only; the widget code was not placed on a site.
claims.buying_consequence: What a real report looks like, and whether the screenshot capture works, is not shown by this test.

claims.observed: The Upgrade page shows the button to upgrade by paying $59 one-time, which matches the dossier price, but the button was not clicked, so no tax, total or payment screen was seen.
claims.plan: No plan was bought; the Upgrade page was read without clicking the $59 button
claims.comparability: The Upgrade page price against a checkout that was not reached; no tax or stored cost rule was compared.
claims.buying_consequence: The amount you would pay in the end, with tax, is not confirmed.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 18 November 2026 the session tested UserHelp.co in our existing free account: a project was made in about a minute and the widget form was previewed, but Submit does nothing in the preview, so no real report was received and the widget was not put on a site. The free plan shows only the 5 oldest responses (the dossier says unlimited), refuses a second project and lists Categories as an upgrade feature, and the Upgrade page shows an Email add-on without a price that the dossier does not have. The price of $59 one-time matches. No plan was bought. Account and start: the test used the existing UserHelp our account, on the Free plan, with the interface in English (the app has no language setting). The test started at 09:01 in our own tab on app.userhelp.co, signed in, with the text Select or create a new project. The dossier name is UserHelp.co and the review is on OSM (userhelp-co-review). UserHelp is a feedback widget that you put on your own site; it is not a help desk or a knowledge base, and no AI assistant was seen in the app. Core action: a project called Test Project Acme was made in 1 step (type a name and press Enter), in about 1 minute, with the message Your new project has been created. The project has the tabs Content, Setup, Responses and Settings. Content has the button text (Report a problem), the button color, text color, Dark mode, a language choice, Add category and a privacy policy URL. The preview of the widget form has Name, Email, Description (required), Capture screenshot, Include my browser details, Submit and the line Powered by UserHelp.co. The preview says that features such as submitting a response and capturing a screenshot are disabled during the preview, and Submit did nothing there, so no real report was received. A real test needs the widget code on a site; that was not done, because the code was not allowed on a site. Setup shows two script lines for the head of a page (run.userhelp.co). Limits on Free: the Responses tab says Only the 5 oldest responses are shown. Upgrade with a one-time payment to view all of them. A second project was refused with an alert that the project limit of the Free account was reached and that unlimited projects need a one-time payment; no second project was made. Plans, read up to the payment step: the Upgrade page (Upgrade your account) lists Unlimited projects (Free accounts are limited to one project), Every response (all of your responses, not just the first 5, and search and filter them), Session replay, Technical details (browser, operating system, error logs, network requests and web vitals), Categories, Team workflow, Public discussions, Integrations (Zapier, webhook) and No watermark, with a button to upgrade by paying $59 one-time. Next to it stands an Email add-on (Email support inbox, Reply notifications, Branded emails, with the line Upgrade your account first to add email features) with no price, and a Lifetime deal box with an LTD code field. Nothing was clicked or filled in. Deviations from the dossier: (a) the dossier says Free has unlimited responses, while the app shows only the 5 oldest on Free. (b) A second project on Free is refused. (c) The dossier puts categories on Free; the app lists Categories as an upgrade feature, although the Add category button is in the Content tab (whether adding a category works on Free was not tried). (d) The Email add-on without a price and the LTD code are not in the dossier. The price of $59 one-time matches the dossier. The number of team members, the retention of recordings, the length of the one-time access and the refund rule are not stated anywhere in the app, which fits the dossier. No price field is changed here. Checkout: NOT reached. The $59 button was not clicked, so no tax, total, card or payment screen was seen. Cancelling: there is no subscription; a project can be removed under Settings, Danger zone, Delete project, which was not clicked, and the profile page only has Log out and Edit profile, with no account deletion. Not tested: a real submission and screenshot (the widget code was not placed on a site), the Pro features, the payment screen, the email functions, the docs site and the terms. Clean up: the project Test Project Acme stays in the account, because Free allows only one project; it can be deleted under Settings. The tab was closed. A first try to make a second project froze the page after the alert; it was restarted by navigating and nothing was made. The profile page, which shows an email address, was not photographed.
exit_test.awkward: Submit does nothing in the preview, so you cannot see what a report looks like without putting the widget code on a site. The free plan shows only the 5 oldest responses and allows one project. Categories appear as an upgrade feature, while Add category stands in the Content tab. The Email add-on has no price on the Upgrade page.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 18 November 2026 the session tested UserHelp.co in our existing free account: a project was made in about a minute and the widget form was previewed, but Submit does nothing in the preview, so no real report was received and the widget was not put on a site. The free plan shows only the 5 oldest responses (the dossier says unlimited), refuses a second project and lists Categories as an upgrade feature, and the Upgrade page shows an Email add-on without a price that the dossier does not have. The price of $59 one-time matches. No plan was bought. Account and start: the test used the existing UserHelp our account, on the Free plan, with the interface in English (the app has no language setting). The test started at 09:01 in our own tab on app.userhelp.co, signed in, with the text Select or create a new project. The dossier name is UserHelp.co and the review is on OSM (userhelp-co-review). UserHelp is a feedback widget that you put on your own site; it is not a help desk or a knowledge base, and no AI assistant was seen in the app. Core action: a project called Test Project Acme was made in 1 step (type a name and press Enter), in about 1 minute, with the message Your new project has been created. The project has the tabs Content, Setup, Responses and Settings. Content has the button text (Report a problem), the button color, text color, Dark mode, a language choice, Add category and a privacy policy URL. The preview of the widget form has Name, Email, Description (required), Capture screenshot, Include my browser details, Submit and the line Powered by UserHelp.co. The preview says that features such as submitting a response and capturing a screenshot are disabled during the preview, and Submit did nothing there, so no real report was received. A real test needs the widget code on a site; that was not done, because the code was not allowed on a site. Setup shows two script lines for the head of a page (run.userhelp.co). Limits on Free: the Responses tab says Only the 5 oldest responses are shown. Upgrade with a one-time payment to view all of them. A second project was refused with an alert that the project limit of the Free account was reached and that unlimited projects need a one-time payment; no second project was made. Plans, read up to the payment step: the Upgrade page (Upgrade your account) lists Unlimited projects (Free accounts are limited to one project), Every response (all of your responses, not just the first 5, and search and filter them), Session replay, Technical details (browser, operating system, error logs, network requests and web vitals), Categories, Team workflow, Public discussions, Integrations (Zapier, webhook) and No watermark, with a button to upgrade by paying $59 one-time. Next to it stands an Email add-on (Email support inbox, Reply notifications, Branded emails, with the line Upgrade your account first to add email features) with no price, and a Lifetime deal box with an LTD code field. Nothing was clicked or filled in. Deviations from the dossier: (a) the dossier says Free has unlimited responses, while the app shows only the 5 oldest on Free. (b) A second project on Free is refused. (c) The dossier puts categories on Free; the app lists Categories as an upgrade feature, although the Add category button is in the Content tab (whether adding a category works on Free was not tried). (d) The Email add-on without a price and the LTD code are not in the dossier. The price of $59 one-time matches the dossier. The number of team members, the retention of recordings, the length of the one-time access and the refund rule are not stated anywhere in the app, which fits the dossier. No price field is changed here. Checkout: NOT reached. The $59 button was not clicked, so no tax, total, card or payment screen was seen. Cancelling: there is no subscription; a project can be removed under Settings, Danger zone, Delete project, which was not clicked, and the profile page only has Log out and Edit profile, with no account deletion. Not tested: a real submission and screenshot (the widget code was not placed on a site), the Pro features, the payment screen, the email functions, the docs site and the terms. Clean up: the project Test Project Acme stays in the account, because Free allows only one project; it can be deleted under Settings. The tab was closed. A first try to make a second project froze the page after the alert; it was restarted by navigating and nothing was made. The profile page, which shows an email address, was not photographed.
exit_test.awkward: Submit does nothing in the preview, so you cannot see what a report looks like without putting the widget code on a site. The free plan shows only the 5 oldest responses and allows one project. Categories appear as an upgrade feature, while Add category stands in the Content tab. The Email add-on has no price on the Upgrade page.
